citation: Cho et al. (2026), High-titer, antibiotic-free, pilot-scale production of 1,3-propanediol by engineered Corynebacterium, Nature Chemical Engineering 3:272–285, DOI 10.1038/s44286-026-00389-w
claim_text: Bounded reconstruction target: reported 1,3-propanediol production result of 141.5 g/L at 2.95 g/L/h without antibiotics.

dependencies.notes: Primary article published 2026-05-12; an author correction on 2026-05-21 changed wording in a toxicity section but explicitly stated that experimental data, results and conclusions were unaffected.
Nature exposes source data and 37 supplementary XLSX datasets; the same study data are deposited at Figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.29264624. Byte-level acquisition/hash remains pending.
Supplementary Information explicitly includes Fermentation Datasets 1–30.
SC97 genome sequencing data are deposited in NCBI.

dependencies.version: GitHub commit 820b43d64f30f6326d5e5d23b38f89bb78355ab3 observed as current repository head
dependencies.notes: SC97-GEM public repository contains the standard and irreversible GEM. Repository history currently shows two commits dated 2026-01-23; no later commit was observed in the initial audit. This computational state is useful for cross-layer provenance but is not required to recompute the bounded fermentation titer itself.
Paper records Aspen Plus version 15 for process simulations; this is relevant to TEA/process conclusions, not required for the bounded titer.

Article identifies the engineered SC97-derived system and antibiotic-free engineering underlying the 141.5 g/L / 2.95 g/L/h result. Exact bounded strain/process dependency graph still requires artifact-level extraction.
Source/fermentation datasets are public, but independent recomputation of the final titer and productivity from released observations has not yet been completed.

findings.evidence: The article abstract explicitly reports 141.5 g/L 1,3-PDO at 2.95 g/L/h without antibiotics.

The paper exposes unusually extensive public source data, Figshare deposition, 30 fermentation datasets, genome sequence and model code; artifact-level mapping to the bounded titer is still in progress.
findings.interpretation: This is currently the strongest positive-reconstruction candidate, but dependency closure should not be asserted before replay.

findings.evidence: A 2026-05-21 author correction changed article text after the 2026-05-12 publication. Current article state is corrected, while the exact original article byte state has not yet been archived by this project.
findings.interpretation: The case demonstrates why publication version/state belongs in scientific provenance even when the correction does not alter the bounded result.

findings.evidence: Public evidence is sufficient to attempt replay, but the 141.5 g/L and 2.95 g/L/h values have not yet been independently recomputed by this project.
findings.interpretation: Keep status pending until reconstruction is executed.
